atoms.a: Why would a semi-colon be used in a sentence?
b: ++to separate two main clauses that are closely linked in meaning

instruction.text: Complete the sentences by adding the correct punctuation.

atoms.b: I desperately need to pack my suitcase((++; --.)) we leave for Cornwall tomorrow((--; ++.))
atoms.sound: I desperately need to pack my suitcase; we leave for Cornwall tomorrow.

atoms.b: The weather has been so unpredictable lately((++; --.)) it’s hard to know whether to bring an umbrella or not((--; ++.))
atoms.sound: The weather has been so unpredictable lately; it’s hard to know whether to bring an umbrella or not.

atoms.b: My grandparents love gardening((++; --.)) they planted a new fig tree last year((--; ++.))
atoms.sound: My grandparents love gardening; they planted a new fig tree last year.

atoms.b: The bus driver wasn’t sure whether there was anyone at the bus stop((++; --.)) the stop was covered by a tree, making it hard to see((--; ++.))
atoms.sound: The bus driver wasn’t sure whether there was anyone at the bus stop; the stop was covered by a tree, making it hard to see.

instruction.text: Drag the semi-colon to the correct place in the text.

atoms.b: We might need to go to the hardware shop((;))we only have one lightbulb left.
atoms.sound: We might need to go to the hardware shop; we only have one lightbulb left.

atoms.b: Most plants need lots of sunlight to grow((;))they struggle in darker rooms.
atoms.sound: Most plants need lots of sunlight to grow; they struggle in darker rooms.

atoms.b: I need to prepare my costume for the school play((;))there’s only a few days left until the premiere.
atoms.sound: I need to prepare my costume for the school play; there’s only a few days left until the premiere.

atoms.b: My brother loves playing computer games((;)) he’s started programming his own recently.
atoms.sound: My brother loves playing computer games; he’s started programming his own recently.
